title: proof_coverage reads a NOTRUN marker: notrun_printed lists those teeth, and no name printed NOTRUN is ever counted green
intention: A proof tooth that needs what a box lacks can print NOTRUN <name> (with a reason). proof_coverage.notrun_printed(stdout) returns those names; teeth_printed keeps its {green, red} shape and never counts a name green if the proof also printed it NOTRUN, and a name printed NOTRUN and red stays red. This is child 1 of ddc5cb6694d3 (D1); the tester honouring it is child 2.
why: Outline 9.4.8.1 (CC's decision on Q#98, after Akien's Q#90 answer, 9.4.2.3.3.1): a tooth that needs what a box lacks reads not-run, never red, its outcome the sealer's. Measured 2026-11-13: nothing reads a not-run marker. teeth_printed reads only GREEN_MARKERS and RED_MARKERS; a line `  NOTRUN  test_x` already mints no tooth (its marker is in neither set), but a name printed both ways (PASS and NOTRUN) would count green, the direction a hollow build wants, and nothing can ask which teeth did not run. A third key in teeth_printed's dict would break the existing equality assertion at test_proof_coverage.py:805 (== {'green': [], 'red': []}), so the shape stays and a new function carries the list.
traces_to: Law 3 (an unmeasured claim is labeled), Law 8 (a hollow green is worse than a red) and Law 9; outline 9.4.8.1.
how: Add NOTRUN_MARKERS = frozenset({'notrun'}) and notrun_printed(stdout) -> list[str], sharing teeth_printed's three line patterns; teeth_printed drops from green any name notrun_printed also names, and red still wins over notrun. Export notrun_printed from the package __init__. Existing outputs with no NOTRUN line read identically.

clauses.claim: notrun_printed returns the names printed on NOTRUN lines, in print order and de-duplicated, and a proof whose only tooth line is NOTRUN has an empty green list from teeth_printed

a name printed both PASS and NOTRUN is not green, a name printed both FAIL and NOTRUN is red and not in notrun_printed, and teeth_printed on output with no NOTRUN line returns exactly what it returned before

decisions.text: D1: NOTRUN_MARKERS and notrun_printed beside teeth_printed; teeth_printed's return shape is unchanged (a third key would break test_proof_coverage.py:805).
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause, over literal stdout strings; red first.

out: the tester (child 2 of ddc5cb6694d3 honours the marker)
converting any proof to print NOTRUN

measured.saw: proof_coverage.py: GREEN_MARKERS = {ok, pass, passed, green, good}, RED_MARKERS = {fail, failed, red, error, errored, broken}; teeth_printed returns {'green': [...], 'red': [...]}; test_proof_coverage.py:805 asserts the exact dict {'green': [], 'red': []}. cairn/devices/tester/device.py:303-305 is the only non-proof caller and reads printed['green'] and printed['red'] only.
measured.how: read proof_coverage.py 60-151; grep -rn teeth_printed over cairn and build_inspector
